title: Compression and the deployment budget
question: When does a smaller weight representation actually fit a device?

sections.heading: Count the entire resident footprint
sections.goal: Calculate whether weight compression brings the entire resident footprint inside a fixed capacity budget, including unchanged activations.
sections.case: Hypothetical inference device: a model has 24 MiB of resident weights and 36 MiB of resident activations; all other memory is excluded from this first accounting. The device allocates 48 MiB to these tensors. A compression method reduces the resident weights to 8 MiB without changing the activations. Treat all quantities as simultaneous resident allocations; do not assume any latency or accuracy improvement. For the transfer, an additional 8 MiB runtime buffer must also be resident and the 48 MiB limit is unchanged.

visual.title: Resident footprint versus capacity
visual.caption: Weights and activations together determine the resident footprint; the compressed case uses {{compressedTotalMiB}} MiB before any extra buffer.

sections.transfer: Now include the additional 8 MiB runtime buffer. Calculate the new resident footprint in MiB and state whether it fits the unchanged 48 MiB budget; explain which allocations you counted.
